title: Invented first consultation: acidity, poor sleep
turns: Good morning. Can you hear me well? Good. So, this is our first consultation. Tell me a little about yourself first. How old are you?
I'm forty-two. I'm a primary school teacher, I teach the third class.
And what brings you to me?
Mostly my stomach, I think. For about two months I get this burning after I eat, like heartburn, and I'm bloated in the evenings. And I'm not sleeping well.
Let's go slowly. What does a normal day of eating look like for you?

Honestly, I skip breakfast most days. I have coffee, maybe three cups before lunch. Lunch is a sandwich at my desk, quickly, between classes. And then dinner is the big meal, usually around nine in the evening, after the kids are in bed.
Yes, a lot. Chilli, curries, and I drink everything cold, even in winter, ice water.
And the burning, when is it worst?
After dinner, and when I eat tomatoes or spicy things. Sometimes it comes up into my throat at night.
Not regular. Sometimes I'm constipated for two or three days, and then it's loose. Well, actually, it's more like every second day, I'd say.
And your sleep? You said it's not good.
I fall asleep fine around eleven, but I wake up at three and then my head starts going, school, lists, and I can't fall back asleep until five or so.
Yes, every twenty-eight days. The first day is quite painful, and it's been heavier for the last half a year.
Two, they're eight and eleven. Both normal births, no complications.
Any allergies? Food that doesn't agree with you?
No allergies that I know of. But milk, I think milk makes me bloated, so I avoid it a bit.
My appendix was taken out when I was nineteen. Nothing else.
And in the family, anything I should know?
My mother has type two diabetes. I'm a little worried about that, but my own blood tests were fine last spring.

Good. Let me tell you what I see. From what you describe, and from your pulse last week, there is a lot of pitta, heat, especially in the digestion. That is the burning and the acidity, what we call amla pitta. And vata is disturbed too: the irregular bowels and waking at three in the morning are typical. By nature I would say you are a pitta vata constitution.
That makes sense, I'm always hot.
So, what I recommend. Every morning, wake up by half past six, scrape your tongue, and drink a glass of warm water before anything else. No coffee on an empty stomach.

One cup, after breakfast, before noon. Through the day drink warm water, about two litres, never ice cold. For the food: no chilli, no tomatoes, nothing fried, and no alcohol for now. Eat a real breakfast, a warm porridge is good, and have dinner before half past seven, and keep it light, soup or rice and vegetables.
Okay, the dinner will be hard but I'll try.

For the acidity I will give you avipattikar churna, half a teaspoon after lunch and after dinner. I also recommend a warm oil massage, abhyanga, once a week for four weeks, and shirodhara for the sleep. For the breath, do sheetali, the cooling breath, ten rounds every evening, and some gentle yoga before bed.
Do I need to come in for all of that?
I suggest an individual programme of twenty-one days, and we review everything in four weeks.
